text: We have been robbed of our clean and green living environment.

text: This is why I do not understand how some political leaders from a neighbouring country can say that they gave us 11 months of fresh air and then we complain about one month of haze.

text: What were the regional and bilateral efforts that Singapore participated or led, in mitigating the causes of the transboundary haze pollution in our region?

text: Would the Minister give us an update on the CV scheme?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: How many had been fined and how many had to perform corrective work orders?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Does the Minister think that corrective work orders and fines have been effective deterrents?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Can NEA look into plans to allocate hawker stalls to applicants from low-income groups and train and equip them with the skills to operate and manage the stalls successfully?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Providing Singaporeans who may have no other skills with a way to earn a livelihood and support their families by running a hawker stall was one of our social objectives in the early days of nation building.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I think this is a valid and viable social objective today and we should continue to provide this means of earning a living to those who need it.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Hawker centres are an essential part of heartland living and part of Singapore's unique national heritage.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Many Singaporeans enjoy our hawker food, its convenience and affordability.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: As many of our hawkers are getting older, how can the Ministry help to preserve the hawker trade?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: How do we ensure that the stall rental prices remain reasonable and the prices of food in our hawker centres remain affordable?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Building the hawker centres is the relatively easier part.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The more difficult challenge is to find enough enterprising hawkers, especially young hawkers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: It is important that we groom a new generation of hawkers so that our hawker culture and the good food can carry on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: To keep our hawker centres vibrant and lively, would NEA consider studying overseas models and experiences, such as those at the Taipei night markets and Hong Kong street markets, to see if there are any good ideas that can be replicated in Singapore?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is to provide a clean, safe and healthy environment for the public and to safeguard their health against the harmful effects of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The last extension of the smoking ban was in 2013.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: While there are recent steps, such as the ban on display at point-of-sale, taken by the Ministry to reduce smoking rates in Singapore, does the Ministry intend to further expand the reach of the smoking ban to cover more places in order to safeguard the health of the public against the harmful and damaging effects of second-hand smoke?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The Active, Beautiful, Clean Waters (ABC Waters) Programme has been well-received by members of the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I was at the launch of the ABC Waters @ Siglap Canal in December last year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Another 54 ABC Waters-certified projects were undertaken by private developers and other public agencies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Ministry elaborate on the plans for the ABC Waters Programme in the next five to 10 years?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I have to add this: if possible, launch one in Nee Soon East.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Yet, we have to provide space for the increasing and much-needed social programmes and services.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Typically, whenever we need more space, we boringly look to void decks and vacant lands.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Yet, we simply do not have enough space to do so.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I believe this challenge is not unique to MacPherson alone.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Faced with this reality, I wonder if we could be more creative and build above the canals?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: By doing so, we can redesign the concept of space.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We will also bridge communities on both sides of the canal and the new space created can be used for eldercare, childcare or for equally meaningful social purposes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: With the canal and water flowing through, beneficiaries and residents can learn about water conservation, the surrounding ecosystem, reclamation of drain and, perhaps, even hydro-power.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We will also be supporting the "A" in the "ABC", as the activities above and around the canal increase.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: One can perhaps draw inspiration from the Lien Foundation project titled "A Different Class: Pre-school Spaces Redefined".

text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister if MEWR will favourably consider such an endeavour for constituencies with canals, such as MacPherson.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, we celebrated SG50 to reflect on our achievements of the past 50 years.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even in our early years, Mr Lee Kuan Yew was already clear that we needed to address poor sanitation, clean our dirty streets, detoxify our polluted rivers.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: His vision was of a clean and green Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It was because of this drive that Singapore became one of the earliest countries in the world to set up a Ministry dedicated to the environment in 1972.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Lim Kim San, the first Minister for the Environment summed up our environmental challenges well.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He said: "Singapore is getting so urbanised that if we don't take action now to keep our environment clean, it will be too late." So, he got to work, and he and the others that came after him, helped to build our City in a Garden that we see today.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: My Ministry conducted a survey in December last year to better understand Singaporeans' perceptions of environmental issues.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The survey shows, among other things, that most respondents continue to recognise that it is everyone's responsibility to deal with the environment and that most view aspects of the environment as important parts of Singapore life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When asked what were the top environmental challenges in Singapore, respondents identified air pollution, cleanliness of public areas and vector-borne diseases as the top three, understandably.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As you can see, almost three-quarters of the Page: 58 respondents considered air pollution as a top challenge.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That is what I will deal with first.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: My Ministry, together with the Ministry of National Development, launched the Sustainable Singapore Blueprint (SSB) 2015 with a holistic vision of a Liveable and Endearing Home, a Vibrant and Sustainable City, and an Active and Gracious Community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It brings together all the things we need to do, so that all of us, whether we are Government, business or people, can work together as one towards a Sustainable Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Under SSB 2015, we have set air quality targets for 2020 and, as Assoc Prof Faishal pointed out, we need to press on with our efforts to reduce local sources of air pollution, as well as carbon, if we are to fulfil our local and international obligations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Studies by the World Health Organization and others have confirmed the harm that air pollution does to our health.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we have systematically introduced policies to reduce air pollution from industries and vehicles.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are the latest international emission standards for petrol and diesel vehicles.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Motorcycles are significant contributors to carbon monoxide and ozone.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are also concerned about emissions from diesel vehicles.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Amid their increasing popularity worldwide, there are increasing concerns about their health and environmental impact.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the wake of the recent Volkswagen scandal, regulators around the world are looking closely at the real world emissions of diesel vehicles, which have been shown to deviate significantly from what is measured in laboratory tests.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to re-look at the widespread use of diesel technology carefully and minimise the public's exposure to risks in the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The results of this study will aid in the review of future vehicular emission policies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Most Singaporeans are only concerned with air quality during haze episodes, especially the PSI shown on their phone apps or on television screens.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is actually a whole team of NEA officers working behind the scenes to keep tabs on the air we breathe in every day.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Those of you who follow my Facebook page would know that since the start of this year, I have been featuring MEWR-family staff under #myMEWRkakis to highlight the work of staff and to show my appreciation to them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Allow me to highlight two more officers here.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Heng Jiarui, a scientific officer, and Ms Fareena Abdul Rahim, a chemical engineer, are both officers in the Pollution Control Department who work closely with their teams to continuously monitor criteria air pollutants from some 22 ambient air quality stations islandwide.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They also monitor 200 sources of industrial emissions for different types of toxic discharges and gases.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If unusual emissions or discharges occur, a response team will have to investigate and stop the discharge.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We can sleep easy at night knowing that these dedicated officers are watching our backs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Page: 59 While we are on the topic of air quality and PSI, I thought it would be a good moment to talk about the haze.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Unfortunately, we are increasingly affected by transboundary haze pollution, as Mr Louis Ng and several Members have highlighted.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last year, we experienced one of the longest haze episodes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is no easy solution to this complex issue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need concerted action by all stakeholders to overcome this problem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the part of the Government, we actively work with our neighbours bilaterally and regionally.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, we will actively promote regional cooperation because haze is a multilateral issue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the haze is largely due to peatland fires, Singapore has facilitated the development of the ASEAN Guidelines on Peatland Fire Management with contributions from all member states.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also host the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre, which helps to monitor the fire and hotspot situation in the region.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This system will need to be supported by effective information exchange among governments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to participate actively in ASEAN initiatives to address transboundary haze and urge all member countries to implement their national action plans and work towards realising the Haze Monitoring System.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, we will continue to support Indonesia's efforts to tackle haze.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, we are addressing the commercial roots of transboundary haze by pursuing errant companies and encouraging the agro-forestry industry to adopt more sustainable practices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Assoc Prof Faishal and Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan have asked about the steps being taken under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA) and other measures to deter errant companies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA is corresponding with them and verifying the information provided.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA is currently reviewing some information received from APPCL.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These Notices require him to provide information and attend an interview in relation to the on-going investigations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In accordance with the law, we will take what steps we can to enforce the THPA, bearing in mind that, outside of Singapore, there are limited possibilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will, of course, hold any Singapore-linked persons or entities to account.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, even if the errant company's officers are foreigners, they will have to comply with the laws of the country, including Page: 60 the Notices under the THPA, should they come to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan has also suggested having settlement agreements and engaging the Law Society for future haze episodes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We could consider these suggestions when we next review the THPA with the experience gained in operationalising it, to see how it can be strengthened to hold errant companies to account – so that people take what we are doing seriously.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Fourth, as consumers, each one of us can influence the agro-forestry industry through our purchasing decisions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last October, the Singapore Environment Council (SEC) suspended the Green Label of APP's exclusive distributor in Singapore and partnered with the Consumers Association of Singapore to advocate for sustainable business practices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Consequently, the larger supermarket chains, such as NTUC FairPrice, Sheng Siong and Prime Supermarket, responded by removing all APP products from their shelves, while the Dairy Farm Group stopped the purchase of all APP products.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our consumers, and consumers all around the world, are rightfully indignant when companies here and abroad blatantly violate their health and well-being with unsustainable practices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These actions demonstrate the significant power of a collective consumer voice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similarly, the Government will be taking the lead in fighting climate change and procure only electrical products that have been certified with high-energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will start with four electrical items − air-conditioners, lamps, televisions and refrigerators – and will gradually extend this to more items.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A silver lining is that civil society and the private sector have stepped up to raise awareness of the sustainability of agroforestry products.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are heartened that WWF-Singapore, PM.Haze and the Singapore Institute of International Affairs jointly organised the "We Breathe What We Buy" campaign to highlight the link between purchasing products made from palm oil from unsustainable sources and the haze episodes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SEC has also announced the expansion of the coverage of the Singapore Green Labelling Scheme to certify products made using sustainable palm oil.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the financial industry, we saw the Association of Banks in Singapore launching its Responsible Lending Guidelines and the Singapore Exchange moving towards its "Comply or Explain" sustainability reporting regime.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are good steps, some maybe baby steps.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope to see more and stronger ground-up initiatives that demonstrate the business case to embrace sustainability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is the sum of all these: regional and international agreements and cooperation, bilateral support, bringing errant companies to task, consumer action, including Government procurement, civil society advocacy, green financing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These will help us edge closer to years in the future without haze.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must press on with our efforts, not just during the haze season, but consistently throughout the year because this is a serious environmental disaster with wide-ranging impact for Page: 61 us now and for the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Irresponsible burning over the years has affected the health of millions of people, impacted regional economies and caused irreversible loss of biodiversity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Singaporeans are, therefore, rightfully outraged because of its health impact; but more than that, the world is rightfully outraged because it also contributes to global warming.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The entire US economy − that is not a small number.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This massive amount of emissions from a single source is a huge setback in our global efforts to combat climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is a good juncture to move on to talk about climate change, which Mr Pritam Singh, Mr Louis Ng and Miss Cheng Li Hui have talked about.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Indeed, while our pioneers were concerned with the environmental impact of urbanisation and dense population to health and hygiene, we are now faced with the impact of climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Climate change will have far-reaching implications on us and future generations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As an island state, we are most vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our delegation, therefore, worked hard to broker consensus on the Paris Agreement so that all countries will take concrete action for it to be effective.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to look systematically at every area while continuing to ensure environmental sustainability, economic competitiveness and energy security.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It also means consumers, households and industries, all of us, need to be prepared to make significant adjustments and trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To reduce emissions, energy efficiency remains our key strategy − we will enhance existing policies and study the introduction of new measures to improve the energy efficiency of industrial equipment and processes, our buildings and transportation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will make up 5% of the projected peak electricity demand.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We cannot over-build because this will incur cost; nor under-build because this will spell disaster.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, the Meteorological Service Singapore has been building up expertise to understand tropical weather at a higher resolution because Singapore is so small that the results from global models would not be meaningful.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Raizan Rahmat, a Senior Research Scientist from the Centre for Climate Research Singapore, and his team worked hard for two years to effectively simulate a hundred years of temperature, rainfall, wind and sea-level projections for Singapore and the region.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Drawing on a range of disciplines such as physics, climate science and atmospheric dynamics, the team developed climate scenarios that were used Page: 62 by our agencies to conduct impact risk assessments and make more informed decisions on how we can bolster our climate resilience.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I wish to share some projections that these studies have made.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Pritam Singh made a suggestion about the possibility of setting up a Climate Change Fund.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government is taking concrete action to prepare for climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have set aside funds for various sectors and agencies to build up capabilities in climate resilience and look at how we can develop more cost-effective solutions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, the Government issued a call for proposals, under the Land and Liveability National Innovation Challenge, for researchers to propose innovative solutions to reduce the ambient temperature in residential estates by four degree Celsius, and that is not just by air-conditioning.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government is mindful of the potential fiscal costs of implementing climate change measures.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we are working with the relevant agencies and MOF to determine the required adaptation plans and financing requirements so that we are well-prepared.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are just some examples of the measures we have taken to safeguard Singapore against rising sea levels.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are confident that Singapore is adequately protected from coastal inundation in the immediate future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To prepare for the longer term, the Building and Construction Authority is conducting a coastal adaptation study which will inform us if additional protection will be needed in the future for our coasts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Government agencies have SOPs and safety guidelines on how to prevent and mitigate heat injury among vulnerable groups, as well as those involved in outdoor activities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government is also undertaking studies to see how we can reduce ambient temperature, whether it is through having more urban greenery, the use of different building materials or the design of developments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah mentioned, rising temperatures also pose an increased and significant threat for vector-borne diseases, like dengue and Zika.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have had more than 6,300 cases in the first three months of this year – more than double that for the same period last year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The recent decrease in cases does not mean that we are safe.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similar to past years, cases may increase as we enter the traditional dengue season in June.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa also mentioned the threat of Zika.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have not seen any cases of Zika so far, but as Singapore is an open and globally connected city, Zika can eventually arrive at our shores.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MOH and NEA have introduced additional surveillance measures.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Zika, like dengue, is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, so the same control measures that we take for dengue also apply to Zika.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, all of us need to step up efforts to eradicate mosquito breeding in our homes and neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our 850 dengue inspectors have also been hard at work.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I highlighted them in my previous posting in myMEWRkakis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While we step up this effort by engaging another 250 temporary officers this year, we are searching for better ways to tackle dengue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our trial to pilot Radio-controlled Aerial Inspection Crafts to aid inspections of roof gutters is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2016.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the longer term, we will need new tools.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA is conducting a feasibility study on the use of Wolbachia-carrying male Aedes mosquitoes to suppress the Aedes mosquito population.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA will conduct a small-scale study involving the release of male Wolbachia-Aedes at the end of the year at a few selected sites.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This study will help us understand the behaviour of these mosquitoes in local conditions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have studied this for years and have taken all steps to ensure that public health and safety will not be compromised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our comprehensive risk assessment has concurred with previous findings on the safety of this technology.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The release of male Wolbachia-Aedes will not pose any risk of biting nuisance or disease, because they are male mosquitoes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will engage residents and stakeholders to provide more information on the technology and the study in due course.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This has impacted the reliability of imported water that supplies half our current needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Fortunately, because we have diversified our water supplies or sources, we have been able to mitigate the impact of the drier weather.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last month, the MIT published a study, which cited that one billion more people in Asia may experience severe water stress by 2050 due to economic and population growth, on top of climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Miss Cheng Li Hui have asked about our long-term plans to ensure water sustainability and drought resilience in the face of climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to plan and invest ahead of demand.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB, the national water agency, has completed its Water Master Plan 2016 review.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Under this Master Plan, PUB will continue to diversify and strengthen our water supply inventory.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB will also be building more desalination plants, on top of the existing two plants.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Construction of the third plant in Tuas is underway and will be completed in 2017.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The fourth plant is planned for in Marina East and, when completed towards the end of 2019, will also strengthen the supply reliability to the city centre.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To further enhance resilience, PUB is exploring the Page: 64 development of a fifth desalination plant on Jurong Island.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB is also planning to harness more seawater as a resource and will work with companies on Jurong Island to meet cooling demand with seawater instead of freshwater supply.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan asked about new advances in water treatment technology.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While we ensure we have enough water, our drinking water must also be clean and wholesome.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is achieved through multiple treatment and control barriers and a source-to-tap water monitoring system, which is supported by a team of 80 water quality professionals trained in disciplines, such as water treatment, microbiology and water chemistry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Three of #myMEWR kakis are shown – Eunice, Yin Mei and Jia Lin.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Each year, PUB conducts over 400,000 tests to ensure that our water is perfectly safe to drink straight from the tap.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: You do not need to boil nor filter it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Louis Ng pointed out, this will pose challenges to flood management.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To prepare for this, PUB has been adopting a holistic "Source-Pathway-Receptor" approach.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This addresses flood protection at all parts of the drainage system.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, PUB requires property developers and owners to implement "source" measures, including detention tanks, to slow down the flow of storm-water run-off into public drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Developers should also implement "receptor" measures, such as higher platform levels, to protect their developments from flash floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While PUB continues to find a balance between minimising flood risks and strengthening drought resilience of our water supply in the face of climate change, we must also minimise leaks and manage our water demand sustainably.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In response to Mr Gan, we are mindful of leakages in our water infrastructure and are required to report to Cabinet periodically on this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has a comprehensive programme to inspect and promptly fix problematic pipes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Both are among the lowest in the world.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: More importantly, everyone has a role to play in preventing water wastage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the years, we have made some progress in water efficiency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As we strive towards the SSB target of 140 litres by 2030, everyone would need to do our part to adopt more water-saving habits and making use of water-efficient technology.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee and Mr Lee Yi Shyan asked about our plan to encourage efficient water use.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB will push for the use of more efficient fittings and appliances.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will implement two measures in early 2017.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, washing machines are labelled with two or three ticks.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The introduction of the 4-tick machines will enable households to Page: 65 select more water-efficient machines from among the current 3-tick models.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are part of our plans to eventually phase out less efficient fittings and appliances by 2018.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will be consulting the industry on these plans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Lee also pointed out that we need to help our commercial water users to use water more efficiently.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Singapore's water demand is projected to double by 2060 and the non-domestic sector will account for 70% of future water demand.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: From January 2015, we have mandated the submission of Water Efficiency Management Plans (WEMP) by large water users.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am heartened that more than 600 large water users have submitted their plans to improve water efficiency and reduce water consumption.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB will study the data collected from WEMP.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will develop water efficiency benchmarks and good practice guidelines, beginning with these big companies and, later on, we will move to the smaller companies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, PUB has been investing in industrial water solutions, such as used water recycling.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since 2006, we have been working with relevant agencies to promote water-related R&D and develop the water industry under the Research Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) plans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to leverage Government schemes where possible, including the RIE2020 plan and the newly-announced industry transformation roadmaps, to foster industry innovation and growth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In Malay):   Over the past 50 years, our pioneer leaders have transformed Singapore into one of the most admired cities in the world.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, challenges, such as climate change, mean that what has worked in the past may not be sufficient for the next 50 years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, how do we protect our coastal areas in the face of rising sea levels?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: How do we deal with issues like dengue, which can spread easily in an increasingly hotter climate?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similarly, the issues of flash floods are expected to become more critical, with more intense rainfall expected in the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need to constantly assess how new global trends and actions of others will affect us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We cannot go about our daily lives as if it were business as usual.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to work with our neighbours and international partners in order to address these problems together.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ultimately, all countries in the world have to ensure that development does not occur at the expense of the environment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I believe that every Singaporean can, and should, step up to do their part to take care of the environment for the future − where our children can lead better lives because of the actions that we take now.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In English): Mdm Chair, in conclusion, I would like to assure Members that my Ministry will strive to uphold the high standards of our environment and water resources we have inherited, even as we face new challenges like climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are doing this not only to benefit Singaporeans now, but also provide a better environment for future generations and the world.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For each one of us, this means living out the beliefs and values underpinning our Sustainable Singapore Blueprint: (a) use only what we need and use it well; (b) care for the place we live; (c) Page: 66 leave something good for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At the same time, it is putting more strain on our already limited resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is, therefore, vital going forward that Singapore and Singaporeans embrace greater environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With limited land, waste reduction is critical to prolonging the lifespan of Semakau Landfill and conserve our land for other uses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is why we have set out a vision of becoming a Zero Waste Nation in the Sustainable Singapore Blueprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Part of our strategy in waste management is to increase the potential for the reuse of incineration ash, which will extend the lifespan of Semakau Landfill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To do this, we must first ensure our waste stream contains as little hazardous substances as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Take the example of electronic waste, or e-waste for short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will only grow as electronic items become more common.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I would also like to touch on a specific hazardous substance, mercury.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Minamata Convention on Mercury is a global, legally-binding instrument that seeks to protect human health and the environment from anthropogenic releases of mercury and mercury compounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In 2013, Singapore signed on to the Minamata Convention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Going forward, we plan to extend the restrictions on mercury content to other products, such as lightings, switches and relays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Another part of our waste management strategy is to work closely with the community and businesses to consume sustainably and reuse and recycle as much as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about the National Recycling Programme (NRP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With the NRP, more than 70% of HDB residents, when asked, said that they practised recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, about 30% to 50% of materials deposited into the recycling bins are not suitable for recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue Page: 67 our efforts to educate the public on what can or cannot be deposited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One area which requires attention is food waste, as pointed out by Dr Chia and Assoc Prof Goh.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is equivalent to two bowls of food per person, per day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is why we launched a programme last November to encourage everyone to reduce food wastage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also want to encourage onsite recycling of food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We launched onsite food waste recycling projects in January this year at two of our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At Hougang Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, Fei Siong Food Management has also voluntarily installed a food waste recycling machine there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These projects will assess the economic and operational aspects of on-site food waste recycling and, if feasible, we plan to roll this out to more of our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Many premises that generate significant volumes of food waste are already doing food waste recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am heartened that about 30 premises, including Resorts World Sentosa, JEM and Singapore Polytechnic, have installed food waste recycling machines at their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In another upcoming pilot project, we plan to start collecting food waste by the end of this year from multiple premises in the Clementi district, including army camps, schools, restaurant clusters, a hawker centre and a hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The food waste will be mixed with used water sludge to enhance energy recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If successful, this could be implemented at the future co-located Integrated Waste Management Facility and the Tuas Water Reclamation Plant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As mentioned by Minister Masagos earlier, our Pioneers worked hard to realise the vision of a clean and green Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In a recent public survey, 95% of Singapore residents agreed that a clean environment, free from litter, is an important part of Singapore's identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Unfortunately, the standard of cleanliness in Singapore continues to be a concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We spend as much as $120 million every year to keep our public spaces clean.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some places, like Orchard Road, have to be cleaned as often as every two hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Over the years, we have stepped up our enforcement against littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We issued more than 26,000 tickets in 2015 – one-third more than in 2014 – and about 1,300 repeat offenders were issued with Corrective Work Order (CWO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While enforcement officers will continue to take action against such irresponsible behaviour, they cannot be everywhere all the time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Er Dr Lee, Mr Gan and Dr Chia have rightly pointed out, keeping Singapore clean requires greater community ownership, such that it becomes part of our local culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The very first "Keep Singapore Clean" campaign was launched by Mr Lee Kuan Yew back in 1968.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This has continued through the years and eventually evolved into the year-long Clean and Green Singapore (CGS) campaign.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The CGS continues to galvanise the community to keep Singapore clean and green, promote the right social values and instil pride in our environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am heartened to see greater community action in keeping our environment clean.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One example is the Public Hygiene Council's tie-up with MOE schools for students to spend five to 10 minutes cleaning their school areas daily, as mentioned by Er Dr Lee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will remind the young to Page: 68 practise consideration and cultivate respect for our cleaners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, the Public Hygiene Council, with the support of NEA, led the "Operation WE Clean Up!".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We want to continue this momentum of ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am pleased to note that the Public Hygiene Council, with the support of the Singapore Kindness Movement and NEA, will lead "Operation WE Clean Up!" 2016 on Sunday, 8 May.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry is also very grateful to the volunteers who are passionate about the environment and have stepped forward to help us raise awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan and Dr Chia asked for an update on the Community Volunteers (CV) programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA's CV programme was started in 2013 to encourage the public to take greater ownership of the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Until recently, only members of a few environment-related NGOs can be part of this programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These volunteers will also be able to take part in a broader scope of environmental education beyond anti-littering efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One of the most common pieces of litter is cigarette butts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Besides contributing to the litter problem, inconsiderate smoking practices also endanger the health of non-smokers through second-hand smoke.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To protect non-smokers, we have progressively prohibited smoking in public places since the 1970s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The smoking prohibition was last extended in 2013 and today, there are more than 32,000 premises and locations where smoking is prohibited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At the same time, the SAF, SPF, SCDF, Prisons, CNB and ICA have, for many years, voluntarily and successfully implemented smoking or smoke prohibition policies within their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will formally include SAF camps and bases and MHA premises to the list of places where smoking is prohibited by law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Dr Chia spoke about the increased rodent population in many estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some 85% of these were found in housing estates managed by Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have also witnessed rat infestations in shopping centres and food establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It remains a challenge for Town Councils in their rodent control efforts, due to the many bin chutes and bin centres and numerous food stalls in the housing estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA has, thus, in late Page: 69 2015, provided funding to support the Town Councils through a revamped Rat Attack programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In areas with multiple stakeholders, actions by one party may displace the rats to another location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, we are taking a more coordinated approach involving multiple stakeholders in a few areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Early results have shown a reduction of rat burrows and we will continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ultimately, the key to managing rat infestation is to remove food sources and areas of harbourage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Stakeholders have a responsibility to improve the housekeeping of their premises, such as bin centres and refuse chutes, and to deny rats easy access to food sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This has to be a consistent and sustained effort by all parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, we tightened the enforcement regime for shopping centres and food establishments with stiffer penalties for repeat offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I will now move on to hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Looking back at the last 50 years, it is amazing how we have successfully turned some of our public health challenges of yesterday into new opportunities for tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The first hawker centres were built in the 1970s to resettle street hawkers and improve hygiene levels by providing access to amenities, such as clean water and proper waste disposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since 2001, over 100 hawker centres have been upgraded under the Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme (HUP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These second-generation centres came with improved ventilation and exhaust system and more dining seats with wider walking space between them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And they were well-received by both hawkers and customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hawker centres are now associated with clean, affordable food and they have become a part of our culture and daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our recent survey found that three out of four respondents visit a hawker centre at least once a week.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry will strive to ensure Singaporeans can continue to have access to a clean environment and affordable food at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan asked about the locations of new hawker centres in Sengkang.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Miss Cheng highlighted the challenge of ensuring that rental remains reasonable and food prices in our hawker centres remain affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry had conducted a study on the drivers of hawker food prices, which former Second Minister Grace Fu shared at last year's Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The study also found that food prices are comparable between subsidised stalls and Page: 70 non-subsidised stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This implies that rental is not the main driver of food prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nevertheless, we have made several changes to help relieve upward pressures on rentals, such as disallowing subletting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since removing the reserve rent in 2012, about 45% of tendered cooked food stalls were awarded at below what the reserve rent would have been.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, more than 85% of our hawkers pay less than $1,500 per month in rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is generally lower than those in coffeeshops or food courts in comparable locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond rentals, we also want to bring in fresh ideas to ensure the sustainability of hawker centres and affordable food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, we have started pilots on new management models at the two new hawker centres at Bukit Panjang and Hougang by appointing social enterprises to manage the centres on a not-for-profit basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will evaluate the outcomes from these pilots to see how we can further enhance the model to achieve our objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Though it is still early days, there are some encouraging takeaways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, the managing agent at Hougang Ci Yuan Hawker Centre has introduced measures to improve productivity, such as self-payment kiosks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They have also introduced an entrepreneurship programme where aspiring hawkers would be given on-the-job training to gain the necessary skills and knowledge to run a hawker stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan also mentioned a previous policy of allocating vacant hawker stalls to those experiencing financial hardship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We had, in the past, offered vacant hawker stalls to people experiencing financial hardship, but the take-up rate was low as most preferred to wait for a vacant stall in popular hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Due to its limited effectiveness, the policy was ceased in 1990.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, anyone interested and who meets the criteria can bid for vacant stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A successful hawker requires both passion and ability and, hence, it is better to let those interested bid for a stall instead of safeguarding them for the low-income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Those who are in financial hardship can be assisted through the various help schemes available, including employment assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: (In Mandarin):   At the Committee of Supply debate last year, my Ministry had announced that the Government would be building 20 new hawker centres by 2027.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During a SGfuture dialogue in January this year, Singaporeans shared their views about the continuity of the hawker trade and the vibrancy of the hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry has, therefore, formed a Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Committee comprises individuals from the community, businesses and Government who take an interest in preserving our hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The committee will look at four issues this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, explore various ways to support new entrants, allow them to operate effectively, thus, sustaining our unique hawker trade in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, propose ideas to improve the productivity in hawker centres to mitigate increases in operating costs and manpower constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, suggest initiatives to enhance hawker centres as a social space for community bonding, which could also improve the vibrancy of hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Page: 71 Fourth, see how there could be ideas to promote graciousness at hawker centres so that hawkers, cleaners and customers can all benefit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: (In English): The Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee has already met a few times since this January.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Er Dr Lee, Mr Liang and Mr Gan asked whether my Ministry is looking to ensure that there are sufficient hawkers equipped with the necessary skills to run the new hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, with the median age of cooked food hawkers at 59 years old, we need to do more to attract new entrants and ensure the sustainability of the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is one of the areas that the committee is looking into.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I recently spoke to Mr Fabian Toh, a third-generation hawker who left his previous job after working for 13 years to take over his family business to sell traditional Chinese dessert at the Chinatown Market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Like many other new entrants, he faced challenges, such as the need to hone his cooking skills and the need to operate during weekends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But many new hawkers also shared that there were some perks, such as having some degree of flexibility in working hours as well as the satisfaction of being commended for their food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to engage these hawkers to find out their motivation for joining the hawker trade, as well as the challenges they face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The committee will explore ideas on how we can attract and, more importantly, support new entrants to the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One idea is through the provision of structured training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some of our hawkers already have innovative ways to improve productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Tan uses a creative but simple machine to automate the frying of traditional Chinese biscuits or 耳朵饼 at his stall in Smith Street Food Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There have also been some ideas on how to enhance the vibrancy of our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One interesting suggestion is to encourage communities to adopt hawker centres and use these spaces for social activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also learn from overseas models and experiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hawker centres have the potential to become great community spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As a continuation of the SGfuture conversation, we will be engaging members of the public for their views.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This year marks the 10th year since our ABC Waters Programme was launched.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Tin asked if we can build above our canals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Where there are opportunities, PUB will work with the relevant stakeholders to add value to the community, without compromising the canal's drainage functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are exciting times as we continue to improve our living environment and transform our urban landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While we see new challenges in the water and environmental space, these also bring about new opportunities and possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have a lot of work ahead of us to build a greener and cleaner Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will work hand-in-hand with the community and all stakeholders in this journey together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And is there any company which takes the easy way out by exiting their businesses in Singapore?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Senior Minister of State mentioned about 20 more ABC Waters projects.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to ensure that these maps are official and they delineate where these occur and who owns these concessions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And because of that, we are working on them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As for the others, we are still working with the Indonesian authorities to make sure what we see on the map, what we see on the satellite, match well with what they have in their records.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: From the speeches on the cuts made by the Members, you can see that hawker centres and ABC Waters projects are much coveted.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Unfortunately, desires are many but resources are limited.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nine are already on-going and there are 10 new upcoming projects.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nee Soon has got two ABC Waters projects: the Seletar Family Bay and Yishun Pond.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee probably has more than some others.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: But my second point was how do we reduce the wastage of food, perhaps by redistributing the food?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I suggested things like incentivising retailers to maybe sell them at a discount or maybe to distribute excess food to charities or similar VWOs.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: The second was, could I have some idea of the efficacy of the Corrective Work Order programme?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Could I find out, of these 1,100, how many actually Page: 73 went into a second repeat?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: What was the recidivism rate of these CWO offenders?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, regarding excess food or unsold food, our strategy towards food waste, first, is not to produce it in the first place.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is the reason why in November last year, we launched the Food Wastage Reduction Outreach Programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under this Food Wastage Reduction Outreach Programme, we were working with many stakeholders to develop good practice guides for food manufacturers, food retail establishments and suppliers to reduce food wastage at source through the supply chain.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also working on a set of food safety guidelines for the safe handling and distribution of unsold and excess food.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are very grateful to NGOs, for instance, Food Bank Singapore and Food from the Heart, who collect and distribute these unsold food to the needy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are coming up with this set of guidelines to support this effort.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also have materials for individuals, to tell them, educate the public that they should only buy or purchase what they can consume.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there are tips and cooking recipes on how to use leftover food.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding CWO, there were 1,300 CWOs in 2015; that was for repeat offenders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Not all the 1,300 recorded in 2015 will tally with the 26,000 because Court orders will take a while so it may be cumulative.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Based on what we have, our analysis is that enforcement, as well as CWOs, are effective because the number of repeat offenders from CWO is very, very small.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First, concerning the haze, the Minister mentioned that we had this earlier collaboration with Jambi province which has ended and we are waiting, I think, for the last four or five years for it to be renewed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Could the Minister share what is holding this up?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Next, regarding dengue, he touched on Radio-controlled Aerial Inspection Craft (RAIC).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Yes, we are aware that the trials are going to end soon.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: My question is whether there is an intention to deploy this on a wider scale and if he can give some information on that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Lastly, I do not think the Minister touched on the issue of the dengue vaccine in his speech earlier.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This Dengvaxia vaccine, I think, has already been registered in a few countries.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I am not sure what is holding the Government up in clearing this vaccine for use in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, it is not our move that terminated the MOU.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Now that we want to resume it, they also have different structures, different people.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Despite promises that they will want to resume it, we have yet to hear from them when and in what form.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And if it works well, together with the possibility of even working with our Malaysian Page: 74 counterpart who has successfully suppressed peatland fires, this can be replicated across Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is, indeed, unfortunate that as enthusiastic as we are to help out our friends, we are not being well responded to.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If it works well, we would be able to deploy it much more widely.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And, of course, this may not be able to be seen.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sometimes, we need the RAIC to see them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just because we can see them and can drop Bti, we should not be doing this every year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We should not be doing this every time, because this, basically, is taxpayers' money.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What owners should do is to take ownership of the problem, repair the problem, solve the problem and prevent the mosquitoes from breeding again.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Next, on the dengue vaccine, we have been closely tracking the development, MOH particularly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need to carefully evaluate whether it is safe.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is new, so we do not know yet whether the quality is what they have promised it to be.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In any case, the company responsible for this vaccine must submit a proposal to HSA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, I think if Members are keen to understand better, best to ask HSA about the vaccine.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I have heard before that some cases got the stalls for single-digit rental; how many of them were there?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Would NEA consider reviving the scheme to allocate hawker stalls to help those in the low-income group who wish to be a hawker to run a hawker stall using all these vacant stalls?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the Sengkang hawker centre, if I remember correctly – and I stand corrected – there may be a wet market, but I will have to check up and confirm.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I can follow up with the Member.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But because we have removed the reserve rent, 45% is actually below what it would have been if there was a reserve rent.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the scheme to help people in financial hardship by safeguarding some stalls, as I have said earlier, we had done this previously.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Based on the experience, what happened was that many of them preferred to wait out for a hawker stall in a popular centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I understand that some could wait for a year, two years or so, and the take-up rate was slow because they only wanted popular locations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Now, anyone who qualifies can bid for a stall, including people who may be interested but are in financial hardship because we have removed the reserve rent.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, he could bid according to what he thinks will be viable for him.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The other thing which is important is that we now give very targeted assistance to people in financial hardship and there are counsellors who will counsel them and identify what their talents, interests and skills are and help them with employment assistance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If, indeed, they are keen to take Page: 75 up hawking, this is also something that the Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee could look into in terms of having some kind of structured training for people who are interested.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You need to give them the right skills so that they can then go and bid for a stall because hawking is not that simple.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do want to help all these people, but we must help them in a targeted manner.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is also about skills, capabilities and business acumen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is important and I think that is the better way to go.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I just want to correct an earlier point.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: About Er Dr Lee's query on new ABC Waters projects.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I said just now there are 20 new projects; nine are ongoing and there are 10 more.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have put it in the media factsheet.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, Members will be able to see it but it has not been publicly announced so I stand to be corrected.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Most of them are in the heartlands and there is actually one project which involves rain gardens in schools.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PUB is working with the schools to encourage the schools to have rain gardens to use it for educational purposes, as well as to encourage the students to appreciate water and learn how to measure water quality, about habitat creation and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the 20 new projects will be: nine on-going, which will be completed over the years; and another 10 new upcoming projects, and one project is the rain garden in schools.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: First is that with the smoking prohibition, does it also cover the parks and public housing estates that are managed by NParks and not just those by the Town Councils?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The second clarification is still on ABC Waters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think the projects you listed are in Nee Soon, but the two are actually not in Nee Soon East.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, I am still hoping the Senior Minister of State will consider Nee Soon East, followed by MacPherson.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The vision of ABC Waters projects is to make the concept and design pervasive in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, integrate it with the adjacent water bodies or have these ABC design features within the development in terms of rain gardens and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If the hon Member has any idea as to where he thinks it is feasible to have an ABC Waters project, he can always propose and we can always look at it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Obviously, resources are limited, but we will look at it with an open view.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, would you like to withdraw the amendment or do you have more requests to make?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Just now, the Senior Minister of State mentioned about Sengkang wet market.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The other clarification is with regard to "no smoking" in the parks.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Why is it not extended to all the parks of Singapore?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because it can be very confusing; certain parks, you allow smoking, certain parks, you do not allow smoking.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And, of course, I support Mr Louis Ng's request for an ABC Waters project in Nee Soon East.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding parks, we will work with the relevant agencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Where there are existing wet markets and we are redeveloping or developing a new one, then there may be a basis for incorporating a wet market to relocate the stalls.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Well, I would also like to request one for my constituency, since a lot of requests are made today.

speaker: The Chairman
text: But anyway Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, do you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And with that, Mdm Chair, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.50 pm.
